interest: Lawyer James Lee Kauffman enlisted Grew and others to fight Japan's 1933 Lawyers' Law restricting foreign attorneys.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This file (decimal file 894.0414) concerns the status of attorneys and the regulation of the practice of law in post-World War II occupied Japan, focusing on efforts by prominent American attorney James Lee Kauffman to re-establish his prewar law firm in Tokyo. Kauffman approached Department of State officials, including Joseph W. Ballantine and Erle R. Dickover of the Far Eastern Commission, to determine whether Japan's prewar 'Lawyers' Law' (Law No. 53 of May 1, 1933) and its 1936 enforcement ordinances restricting alien legal practice remained on the books or had been abrogated by the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP). In reply, U.S. Political Adviser George Atcheson, Jr. reported from Tokyo that the 1933 statute and its strictly interpreted reciprocity provision under Article 6 remained in force, having historically permitted only three foreign practitioners (John Gadsby, William J. Sebald, and Arthur M. Spencer) to secure limited licenses. The correspondence extends into late 1949, when former Ambassador Joseph C. Grew intervened with Assistant Secretary of State W. Walton Butterworth on Kauffman's behalf, transmitting his formal application to the Secretary of the Army and supporting documentation highlighting his prewar leadership of the American Association of Japan.

subfiles.about: Report on the statutory history of the Japanese Lawyers' Law and verification of its status in the Kampo official gazette.
subfiles.summary: Henry L. Trepagnier, Jr. tells Dickover Japan's 1933 Lawyers' Law and 1936 ordinances on alien lawyers have not been repealed.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Trepagnier to Dickover regarding Lawyers' Law

subfiles.about: Inquiry into whether Japan's Lawyers' Law has been repealed and thoughts on the resumption of American business in Japan.
subfiles.summary: James Lee Kauffman asks Ballantine whether Japan's Lawyers' Law has been repealed, hoping to reopen his Tokyo practice.
subfiles.title: Letter from Kauffman to Ballantine regarding Japanese Lawyers' Law and Reopening Legal Practice

subfiles.about: Inquiry addressed to the U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo regarding the status of Japanese laws restricting foreign attorneys.
subfiles.summary: Dickover asks Atcheson whether SCAP or Japan plans action on the 1933 Lawyers' Law, relaying Kauffman's wish to reestablish his Tokyo firm.
subfiles.title: Letter from Dickover to Atcheson regarding Inquiry on Lawyers' Law

subfiles.about: Interim reply informing Kauffman that inquiries regarding the Lawyers' Law have been forwarded to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Dickover tells Kauffman the 1933 Lawyers' Law appears unrepealed and that he has asked Atcheson in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Letter from Dickover to Kauffman regarding Status of Lawyers' Law

subfiles.about: Acknowledgment of Dickover's update and recollection of assurances given by Civil Affairs Training School officers.
subfiles.summary: Kauffman recalls Civil Affairs Training School officers promising early repeal of the Lawyers' Law and awaits Atcheson's reply.
subfiles.title: Letter from Kauffman to Dickover regarding Revocation of Lawyers' Law

subfiles.about: Report confirming that Japan's 1933 Lawyers' Law and strict reciprocity requirements remain in force.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson reports the 1933 Lawyers' Law remains in force; strict reciprocity meant only three foreign attorneys were ever licensed.
subfiles.title: Letter from Atcheson to Dickover regarding Status of Law No. 53 of 1933

subfiles.about: Transmission of James Lee Kauffman's application to the Department of the Army to practice law in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Grew forwards to Butterworth James Lee Kauffman's application to the Army to practice law in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Grew to Butterworth enclosing Kauffman's Application to Practice Law

subfiles.about: Acknowledgment of receipt of Kauffman's application materials regarding legal practice in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Butterworth acknowledges Grew's letter enclosing Kauffman's application to practice law in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Butterworth to Grew acknowledging Kauffman Application

subfiles.about: Transmittal to Kauffman of George Atcheson's report explaining that Japan's restrictive Lawyers' Law remains unrepealed.
subfiles.summary: Dickover sends Kauffman Atcheson's report that the 1933 Lawyers' Law remains intact, noting repeal of such laws will take time.
subfiles.title: Letter from Dickover to Kauffman enclosing Atcheson's Report on Lawyers' Law
